import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

## Summary

Completed the `ack` phase of epic `sase-l1`: the supervisor now writes a `.monitor_started` marker (real pid/pgid/identity/monitor_id) before waiting on the launch barrier, and `start_monitor` blocks on it (20s budget), polling supervisor liveness so a dead pid fails fast. On timeout or death it terminates the supervisor, hands the workspace claim back to the still-live starter exactly as held (never releasing into the free pool), tears the member down as terminal `failed`, and raises `MonitorError` — fixing the exact incident this epic exists for.

Beyond the initial implementation (which a prior, terminated session had left uncommitted and untested), I found and fixed real regressions:
- Two existing test fixtures that faked the supervisor spawn without acknowledging it — the new blocking wait turned these into a 20s hang or, worse, a self-SIGTERM of the pytest process itself (the fake pid coincided with the test process's own pid).
- A `detach`-phase test whose SIGTERM-during-startup race was defeated by the new blocking wait; rewrote it to deliver the signal from a background thread the moment the supervisor's pid lands on disk.
- Added 3 new tests covering the ack marker's contents, the dead-on-arrival scenario, and the ack-timeout scenario, split into a new `test_monitor_start_ack.py` since `test_monitor_start.py` was already near the repo's 1000-line lint cap.

Verified via `tests/monitor/` (117 passed), ruff, mypy, and `just lint` (clean). `just check`'s full parallel suite hit a merge conflict against a concurrently-landed sibling phase (`followup`) touching the same test file, which I resolved by merging both sides' imports — re-verified afterward. Two unrelated pre-existing failures in `tests/plan_show/test_resolve.py` (confirmed failing on clean master) and 3 timing-flaky assertions in `test_monitor_supervise.py` under parallel load were recorded as `PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP` notes on the bead. Commit `b4542139a` is pushed and the bead is closed.
